title: Synthetic EHR Generators Should Be Audited Like LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2611.28804v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Synthetic electronic health record (EHR) generation is increasingly adopting large autoregressive models, yet privacy evaluation has not kept pace, relying heavily on similarity-based heuristics and aggregate metrics that can obscure patient-specific memorisation. We argue that these models should additionally undergo LLM-style memorisation audits at the level of individual patient records. We support this position by comparing membership-inference evaluations across four prominent autoregressive EHR generators, highlighting inconsistent evaluation practices in patient representations and attack procedures. We evaluate trajectory reconstruction from partial context and introduce randomly assigned patient-level canaries to distinguish memorised associations from clinical generalisation. translated_title: 合成电子健康记录生成器应像大语言模型一样接受审计
translated_abstract: 合成电子健康记录（EHR）生成技术正日益采用大型自回归模型，然而隐私评估却未能跟上步伐，严重依赖基于相似性的启发式方法和聚合指标，这些方法可能掩盖针对特定患者的记忆化现象。我们主张，这些模型还应像大语言模型一样，在单个患者记录层面接受记忆化审计。我们通过比较四个知名自回归EHR生成器的成员推理评估来支持这一观点，揭示了患者表示和攻击程序方面不一致的评估实践。我们评估了从部分上下文重建患者轨迹的方法，并引入随机分配的患者级金丝雀（canary）样本，以区分记忆化的关联与临床泛化。我们在一个刻意对1,000条MIMIC-IV患者轨迹过拟合的GPT-2风格模型中检验了这些方法，创建了一个可控的实验环境来研究记忆化行为。
tldr: 本文主张合成EHR生成模型应在单个患者记录层面接受类似大语言模型的隐私记忆化审计，并通过成员推理评估、轨迹重建和随机患者级金丝雀样本等方法，在过拟合的GPT-2风格模型上验证了这一审计框架的必要性。
en_tdlr: Synthetic EHR generators should undergo LLM-style memorisation audits at the individual patient record level, demonstrated through membership-inference evaluations, trajectory reconstruction from partial context, and randomly assigned patient-level canaries to distinguish memorisation from clinical generalisation.
